title: Ruler-boundary test machine
statement: There exist a finite state set $P$, a deterministic one-work-tape binary Turing machine $R$, entry and distinct yes/no states, and a constant $C$. For every binary input $z$, ruler length $\ell>0$ not exceeding the input-head position, and configuration $d$ in the entry state whose work tape contains a ruler of $\ell$ ones at offsets $-1$ through $\ell$, the machine reaches within $C(\ell+1)$ steps the configuration identical to $d$ except that its state is yes exactly when the input-head position equals $\ell$, and no otherwise. It visits neither yes nor no earlier, and its work-head displacement at every time up to arrival has absolute value at most $\ell+1$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite state type P with decidable equality
A deterministic one-work-tape binary machine R
Entry, yes, and no states, with yes distinct from no
A binary input z, ruler length ℓ, and configuration d
The ruler length ℓ is positive and at most the input-head position
The ruler tape agrees with the length-ℓ buffer tape at offsets −1 through ℓ
